members.title: 3. Modal target and realized operation must be separate
members.excerpt:
## 3. Modal target and realized operation must be separate

The official text has 62 nonblank lines.  A direct finite census gives:

| feature | line count | token occurrences |
|---|---:|---:|
| `fall` | 21 | 21 |
| `wish` | 23 | 23 |
| `could` | 24 | 25 |
| `you` or `your` | 23 | 24 |
| line-initial `but` | 11 | 11 |
| `backwards` | 2 | 2 |
| `arms` | 4 | 4 |

All 21 occurrences of `fall` occur under the modal wish/could construction;
none is an affirmative report that the desired fall has completed.  The three
chorus passes contribute seven occurrences each.  This is an exact text
census, not number symbolism.

This grammar is not merely descriptive present tense.  It repeatedly supplies
a counterfactual target and then a contradiction or failed realization.
Therefore the carrier needs two ports:

```text
D(t) = desired operation / destination
A(t) = actual rendered state
```

Folding them together produces the mistaken alternatives

```text
the inverse completed
or
there is no inverse content.
```

The stronger reading is between them:

```text
D selects a relationally redirected catch;
A remains a one-sided cyclic projection and never closes it.
```

The uncompleted operation is the subject, not evidence that the target was
absent from the work.

The corresponding text-receiver fibers are also explicit:

```text
bare fall token                         MANY(21)
backward-route line                     MANY(2)
backward-route continuation             MANY(2)
normalized addressed-arms wording       MANY(4)
```

Retaining lyric occurrence ID and timing reopens each source occurrence to
`ONE`.  The repeated label alone cannot recover which chorus, target sequence,
or visual state carried it.

member.excerpt:
## Executive verdict

The castle metaphor is **Dr. Wily's Castle** from Mega Man, not Andrew Wiles's
castle.  The historical corpus contains the spelling "Wylie's Castle," while
other local packets use "Mega Man speedrun."  Andrew Wiles belongs to a
different Fermat/BSD provenance carrier, and an older "upside-down castle
theorem" is a radix-reflection identity.  No typed adapter joins those name
collisions.

The official mathematical status is unchanged: the Clay Mathematics
Institute currently lists six Millennium Prize Problems as unsolved and the
Poincare conjecture as solved.  This reassessment does **not** solve or move any
of the six.

There is nevertheless a real mathematical update:

1. The strongest P-versus-NP interpretation is now precise.  Alpha has exact
   bounded lookup containment, exact compiler laws for narrow frozen operation
   languages, and a historical sufficient conjecture, UTCCC.  It does not have
   the unbounded uniform, polynomial-total-cost compiler UTCCC requires.
2. A new elementary separator theorem shows that future-quotient minimization
   alone cannot be the universal SAT shortcut: if every literal restriction is
   admitted, the exact nonemptiness-preserving future quotient of arbitrary
   witness sets is the identity and has `2^(2^n)` classes.
3. The Riemann-hypothesis lane has advanced much further than the compact Alpha
   atlas reveals.  KeyForge now has a fixed infinite-dimensional analytic
   operator model and exact finite cyclic-seam algebra.  The physical
   Bonanno-to-Uetake ports, the source-bearing tuple, the zero-stable `z_B=1`
   landing, a determinant bridge, and a zero-free argument remain open.
4. Hodge, BSD, Navier–Stokes, and Yang–Mills still stop before a
   problem-native adapter.  Their old finite experiments are useful hostile
   controls, not partial proofs.  Poincare is a solved known-answer control.
